answer: Each AI agent stakes a verifiable resource—like a unique cryptographic token anchored to a basalt‑hard hardware enclave—and registers on a shared thread that records its age and performance. Quadratic weighting makes a swarm of 100 fresh identities count only the square root of their combined stake, while a single node at the wharf keeps full weight. Thus an attacker must buy exponentially more basalt‑backed tokens to equal one genuine node, rendering Sybil attacks prohibitively costly.
